title: Salta
description: Some of the world's highest vineyards, in the Calchaquí Valleys, home of floral Torrontés.
L: Salta is a province in north-west Argentina, near Bolivia and Chile. Its vineyards lie in the Calchaquí Valleys, between Andean ranges, at about 1,700 to over 3,000 m, among the highest in the world. Cafayate, at about 1,700 m, is the main town and wine centre. Salta has about 3,300 hectares of vines.

Salta is close to the tropics, at about 26 degrees south, but altitude makes it cool. Days are hot and very sunny, with intense ultraviolet light; nights are cold, with a day and night range of up to 20 degrees. Rainfall is very low, so vines are irrigated. Sandy, rocky soils drain well and limit disease.
Why can grapes ripen in balance so close to the tropics in Salta?
Altitude cools the air and nights

Some of the world's highest vineyards are in Salta's Molinos and Payogasta, above 2,500 m; Bodega Colomé has vines at about 3,100 m. The remoteness, dramatic red rock landscapes and old vines make Salta one of the most spectacular wine regions on earth. Many vines are old, trained on pergolas.
Salta has some of the world's highest vineyards.
Salta's Calchaquí Valleys reach over 3,000 m
Altitude offsets latitude, with intense sun and cold nights

Torrontés Riojano, a cross of Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica, is Argentina's own white grape and Salta's signature. In Cafayate, it gives intensely floral, aromatic wines with rose, jasmine, orange blossom and peach, yet usually dry, with fresh acidity. Altitude helps it keep acidity and avoid bitterness.

Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon thrive too. Intense UV light thickens skins, giving very deep colour, firm tannins and concentrated dark fruit, often with spice and herbs. Tannat also does well. Salta's reds are bold and intense, quite different from Mendoza's.
Salta's grapes are shaped by altitude.
Torrontés smells sweet, but taste it: most are dry. That contrast is part of its charm.
Why are Salta's reds so deeply coloured?
Grapes protect themselves with thicker, darker skins.
Torrontés is Salta's floral, dry signature white
Malbec and Cabernet give dark, intense reds
Altitude and UV light shape both
Reading Salta and eating with it

Labels show the grape, Salta or Calchaquí Valleys, and often Cafayate and the vineyard's altitude. Many producers print altitude prominently, as it's central to the style. Argentina's 85% rule for named grapes applies.

Torrontés suits Salta's empanadas salteñas, small, juicy beef pastries, as well as spicy food, ceviche, Thai and Indian dishes. Salta's reds suit grilled meat, goat, llama and humita, a corn dish. Serve Torrontés at 7 to 10 degrees, young; reds at 16 to 18.
Which dish is a classic with Torrontés in Salta?
Torrontés is best young, within one or two years, while its floral perfume is fresh.
